issues.description: The template implementation of simulate_ghz_state in tensor_networks.py is missing the shots parameter in its signature, while the problem statement and the reference solution expect simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits, shots). The template's function body and assertions even reference shots (e.g., assert shots > 0), creating a clear mismatch between the function signature and its intended usage. This will prevent students from implementing or calling the function as specified in the exercise and will cause confusion and runtime errors when they follow the problem description or run tests that pass shots.
issues.suggested_fix: Modify the template function signature to include the shots parameter to match the problem statement and solution: def simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits: int, shots: int) -> dict[str, int]. Update the docstring and ensure any internal assertions/reference to shots are consistent. This aligns the template with the intended API used by the tests and the reference implementation.
